title: 6. Data Transformation & Log Scaling
description: Transform heavily skewed data with log scaling, binning, and one-hot encoding.

blocks.content:
### Log Transformation & Encoding

When numeric features have a long right tail (skewed distributions like income or house prices), applying `np.log1p()` compresses extreme values and normalizes the distribution.

![Log Transform Comparison](/images/ml/chart_log_transform.png)

#### One-Hot Encoding
Converts categorical strings into binary indicator columns ($0$ or $1$) so mathematical models can consume them:

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'color': ['Red', 'Blue', 'Green']})
df_encoded = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=['color'])
print(df_encoded)
```

blocks.question: Why is np.log1p(x) preferred over np.log(x) when performing log transformations on real-world datasets?
options: np.log1p(x) calculates log(1 + x), avoiding errors when encountering zero values
np.log1p(x) only works on string data
blocks.explanation: log(0) is undefined (-infinity). np.log1p(x) computes log(1 + x), safely handling zero values.
